homonyms.basis: The census rows carry no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym, and T composes no other entity under the name. 'The NEXT: Museum, Library, and Preservation Space' and 'The NEXT Museum' are the entity's fuller names (the authorship census's aka; Wikipedia's title); the-next.org and the-next.eliterature.org are its hosts. 'next' alone is a common word and is not a name of the entity. The distinct entities below are named by the field, the censuses or the archive beside the entity and are never senses of its name.
distinct_entities: the Electronic Literature Organization (eliterature.org, card 1), whose museum The NEXT is (F2, F44): an organization distinct from it
the ELO Repository (archive.the-next.org, B7), which names The NEXT and holds collections 'coming soon' to it: 'NOT the ELO Repository' (LS-26)

the Electronic Literature Lab at Washington State University Vancouver, which manages it and holds its physical artifacts: 'NOT the Electronic Literature Lab' (LS-27), a row of the authorship census of its own
the Electronic Literature Collections (ELC), anthologies among its holdings (F14, F47); the layer census's relation has_part
the Electronic Textual Cultures Lab at the University of Victoria and Compute Canada, which hosted it at its seeding (F29)
the ELMCIP Knowledge Base, which lists its exhibition afterflash (B10, TLL-19), a neighbour in the layer census
the Electronic Literature Foundation, named in #301 beside Glazier as a site of digital poetics: an organization distinct from the ELO
Marjorie C. Luesebrink and M.D. Coverley: one person and her pen name (F62, F46), an author held in the museum and never the museum
Katya Farinsky, the author of card 3's portfolio page, the project's copyeditor and copywriter (F25)

captures.description: THE MUSEUM, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The NEXT is a digital art and writing museum, library, and preservation space created by the Electronic Literature Organization (ELO).' Key details: purpose ('Maintains and shares the cultural record of born-digital human expression'), contents ('over 3,000 born-digital literary works and dozens of collections ... dating from the mid-1980s onward'), support (the Electronic Literature Lab 'alongside the ELO'), leadership (Dene Grigar); two follow-up offers, the first to 'Search for a particular author or artist in the archive'. Six cards: the ELO, the-next.org (three), katyafarinsky.com, a YouTube talk by Dene Grigar.
